name: Core Rehabilitation Program
description: A comprehensive 18-week abdominal rehabilitation program designed to progressively rebuild core strength, stability, and functional movement patterns.

weeks.educationalContent: Your core is more than just your abdominal muscles. It includes the deep stabilizers that support your spine, pelvis, and breathing. This week focuses on reconnecting with these muscles through gentle activation and awareness exercises.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Establish a daily rehabilitation routine and become aware of your core engagement patterns throughout the day.

activities.name: Gentle Core Activation
activities.description: Lying on your back, gently draw your navel toward your spine without holding your breath.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent. Place hands on lower abdomen. Gently draw your belly button toward your spine. Hold for 5 seconds, release. Focus on the feeling of gentle engagement.

tips: Keep breathing normally throughout
The movement should be subtle — not a strong contraction
Place a small towel under your head if needed
modifications: If lying flat is uncomfortable, use a pillow under your knees
Can be performed seated if needed

activities.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
activities.description: Deep belly breathing to engage the diaphragm and coordinate with core activation.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back with one hand on your chest, one on your belly. Breathe in through your nose — your belly should rise while your chest stays relatively still. Exhale slowly through pursed lips. Focus on the gentle expansion and contraction.

tips: Inhale for 4 counts, exhale for 6 counts
Your belly hand should move more than your chest hand
Practice in a quiet, calm environment
modifications: Can be performed seated or semi-reclined
Use a pillow under knees for comfort

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Gentle walking at a comfortable pace to promote circulation and gentle core engagement.
activities.instructions: Walk at a comfortable pace on a flat surface. Focus on upright posture and gentle core awareness. Stop if you feel any discomfort.

tips: Walk at a pace where you can still hold a conversation
Focus on posture — shoulders back, chin level
Wear supportive shoes
modifications: Break into two 5-minute walks if needed
Indoor walking is perfectly fine

activities.name: Posture Check
activities.description: Three times today, stop and check your posture. Are you aligned? Is your core gently engaged?
activities.instructions: Stand tall. Imagine a string pulling you up from the crown of your head. Relax your shoulders down and back. Gently engage your core. Hold this awareness for 30 seconds.

tips: Set reminders on your phone
Check posture when transitioning between activities
Good posture should feel natural, not forced
modifications: Can be done seated — focus on sitting tall

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: If you are using a support garment, ensure it is positioned correctly and at the right tension.
activities.instructions: Check that your support garment is positioned correctly — centered over your midline, providing gentle compression without restricting breathing. Adjust if needed.

tips: The garment should feel supportive, not restrictive
You should be able to breathe normally
Reposition after any physical activity
modifications: Skip if not using a support garment

weeks.educationalContent: The connection between your brain and your core muscles may need rebuilding. This week adds coordination exercises that train your nervous system to properly activate deep core muscles during everyday movements.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Improve mind-muscle connection and maintain consistent daily practice.

activities.name: Core Activation with Breath
activities.description: Coordinate core engagement with your breathing pattern for deeper activation.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent. Inhale to prepare. As you exhale, gently draw your navel toward your spine and hold for 5 seconds. Inhale to release. Repeat.

tips: Exhale as you engage, inhale as you release
Keep the movement controlled and smooth
Your lower back should maintain its natural curve
modifications: Use a pillow under knees if needed

activities.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
activities.description: Continue building your breathing practice with slightly longer exhales.
activities.instructions: Same position as Week 1. Inhale for 4 counts through your nose. Exhale for 7 counts through pursed lips. Focus on complete, slow exhalation.

tips: The longer exhale helps activate your deep stabilizers
Keep your jaw and shoulders relaxed
Practice before bed for better sleep
modifications: Reduce exhale count if 7 is too long

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Continue daily walks with increased awareness of posture and core engagement.
activities.instructions: Walk at a comfortable pace for 12 minutes. Maintain upright posture and gentle core awareness throughout.

tips: Gradually increase pace if comfortable
Swing arms naturally
Breathe rhythmically
modifications: Break into shorter segments if needed

activities.name: Body Mechanics Practice
activities.description: Practice proper lifting and bending techniques using your core.
activities.instructions: Practice the hip hinge: stand with feet hip-width apart, engage your core, and bend forward from your hips (not your waist) while keeping your back straight. Return to standing by squeezing your glutes and using your legs.

tips: Imagine you're closing a car door with your hips
Keep your core engaged throughout
Practice with light objects first
modifications: Hold onto a counter for balance

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Daily check of support garment positioning.
activities.instructions: Verify positioning and tension of your support garment. Adjust as needed.

tips: Check after meals and physical activity
modifications: Skip if not using a support garment

weeks.educationalContent: Your body adapts to consistent practice. This week we gently increase the challenge while maintaining proper form. Quality of movement always matters more than quantity.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Increase exercise volume slightly while maintaining perfect form and breathing coordination.

activities.name: Core Activation Hold
activities.description: Extended holds to build endurance in your deep core muscles.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent. Engage your core as practiced. Hold for 8 seconds, rest for 5 seconds. Repeat. Focus on maintaining steady breathing throughout the hold.

tips: Breathe normally during holds
If you can't maintain the hold without holding your breath, reduce the time
Quality over quantity
modifications: Start with 5-second holds and build up

activities.name: Seated Breathing Exercise
activities.description: Practice diaphragmatic breathing in a seated position to transfer skills to daily life.
activities.instructions: Sit tall in a chair with feet flat on the floor. Place hands on your belly. Practice the same breathing pattern — inhale 4 counts, exhale 7 counts — while maintaining upright posture.

tips: This transfers your practice to real-life positions
Keep your spine tall but natural
Relax your shoulders away from your ears
modifications: Use a supportive chair with good back support

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Increase walking duration with conscious core engagement.
activities.instructions: Walk for 15 minutes at a comfortable-to-moderate pace. Every 5 minutes, do a mental posture check: shoulders back, core gently engaged, breathing steady.

tips: Try to walk on varied terrain if comfortable
Include gentle inclines if available
Stay hydrated
modifications: Break into three 5-minute walks

activities.name: Posture Awareness
activities.description: Extended posture practice integrated into daily activities.
activities.instructions: Choose three daily activities (eating, working, watching TV) and practice maintaining proper posture throughout. Set a timer for 5 minutes of focused posture awareness during each.

tips: Link posture checks to existing habits
Good posture should eventually feel automatic
Take breaks from prolonged sitting
modifications: Start with 2-minute intervals

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Daily support garment check.
activities.instructions: Verify positioning, adjust tension as your body changes.

tips: Your needs may change as you progress
modifications: Skip if not using a support garment

weeks.educationalContent: Stability is the ability to maintain control during movement. This week introduces exercises that challenge your core to stabilize while your limbs move — a fundamental skill for everyday life.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Begin stability exercises while maintaining breathing coordination and proper core engagement.

activities.name: Heel Slides
activities.description: Maintain core stability while slowly sliding one heel along the floor.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent. Engage your core. Slowly slide one heel along the floor until the leg is almost straight, then slide it back. Keep your pelvis completely still throughout. Alternate legs.

tips: Your pelvis should not rock or tilt
Move slowly and with control
Keep breathing throughout
modifications: Reduce range of motion if pelvis moves
Place hands on hip bones to monitor stability

activities.name: Extended Breathing Practice
activities.description: Longer breathing sessions to deepen relaxation and core coordination.
activities.instructions: Choose a comfortable position. Practice diaphragmatic breathing for a full 5 minutes. Focus on the rhythm: inhale 4, exhale 7. Let tension dissolve with each exhale.

tips: Use this as a stress-relief tool
Practice at the same time each day
Close your eyes for deeper focus
modifications: Start with 3 minutes and build up

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Maintain 15-minute walks with improved posture awareness.
activities.instructions: Walk for 15 minutes. Focus on walking tall, engaging your core gently, and maintaining smooth, even strides.

tips: Try different routes to stay motivated
Walk with a friend for accountability
Notice how your posture affects your energy
modifications: Adjust pace as needed

activities.name: Functional Movements
activities.description: Practice getting up from a chair and bending with proper core support.
activities.instructions: Practice sitting down and standing up from a chair 10 times using proper body mechanics: core engaged, hinge at hips, use leg strength. Then practice picking up a light object from the floor using a proper squat or lunge pattern.

tips: Never hold your breath during these movements
Think 'core first, then move'
Use armrests for support if needed
modifications: Use a higher chair if needed
Pick up objects from a table instead of the floor

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Daily support garment check.
activities.instructions: Check and adjust your support garment.

tips: Ensure garment stays in place during exercises
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: As your core foundation strengthens, we can safely expand the range of motion in exercises. Greater range means greater challenge — but always within your comfort zone. Listen to your body.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Increase exercise range of motion and duration while maintaining quality form.

activities.name: Marching in Place
activities.description: Lift alternate knees while lying down, keeping your core stable and pelvis neutral.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent. Engage your core. Slowly lift one foot off the floor, bringing your knee toward your chest to about 90 degrees. Lower slowly. Alternate sides. Keep your lower back pressed gently into the floor.

tips: Move slowly — speed is not the goal
Your back should not arch
Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower
modifications: Reduce height of knee lift if needed

activities.name: Breathing with Movement
activities.description: Coordinate breathing with gentle arm movements to build dynamic breath control.
activities.instructions: Sit or stand tall. Inhale as you slowly raise both arms overhead. Exhale as you lower them. Coordinate the movement with a 4-count inhale and 6-count exhale. Keep your core gently engaged throughout.

tips: Arms move with the breath, not independently
Keep shoulders relaxed
Focus on smooth, continuous movement
modifications: Raise arms only to shoulder height if needed

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Increase walking duration to 18 minutes with core awareness.
activities.instructions: Walk for 18 minutes at a moderate pace. Include gentle arm swings. Maintain core engagement and upright posture throughout.

tips: Add a gentle incline if available
Focus on heel-to-toe stride
Enjoy the outdoors if possible
modifications: Break into two 9-minute walks

activities.name: Standing Core Engagement
activities.description: Practice engaging your core during standing activities.
activities.instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart. Practice engaging your core while performing daily tasks: washing dishes, brushing teeth, waiting in line. Hold engagement for 10-second intervals.

tips: This builds functional strength
Integrate into your daily routine
Don't hold your breath
modifications: Lean against a counter for support

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Daily support garment check.
activities.instructions: Check positioning and comfort. You may notice less reliance on the garment as your strength improves.

tips: Discuss garment use with your healthcare provider
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: Endurance means your muscles can work for longer periods without fatigue. This week extends hold times and adds repetitions. Consistency is building real change in your body — even if you can't see it yet.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Build muscular endurance through longer holds and additional repetitions.

activities.name: Extended Core Holds
activities.description: Longer holds with controlled breathing to build deep core endurance.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent. Engage your core and hold for 10 seconds. Rest 5 seconds. Repeat. Maintain steady breathing throughout each hold.

tips: If you can hold easily for 10 seconds, you're ready for this
Focus on consistent engagement — no flickering
Count your breaths during holds
modifications: Reduce to 8-second holds if needed

activities.name: 360-Degree Breathing
activities.description: Expand your breathing to fill your ribcage in all directions.
activities.instructions: Sit or lie with a resistance band loosely around your lower ribs. Breathe in and try to expand the band in all directions — front, sides, and back. Exhale slowly. This teaches full ribcage expansion.

tips: You don't need a band — just imagine one
Feel for expansion in your back ribs
This is advanced breathing — be patient
modifications: Place hands on your side ribs to feel expansion

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Increase walking to 20 minutes at a moderate pace.
activities.instructions: Walk for 20 minutes. Maintain good posture and gentle core engagement. Try to include one gentle hill or incline if available.

tips: 20 minutes is a great habit to maintain
Vary your routes for interest
Walking after meals aids digestion
modifications: Split into two 10-minute walks

activities.name: Lifting Mechanics
activities.description: Practice proper lifting technique with light household items.
activities.instructions: Practice lifting a light bag or book from the floor: engage core first, squat with knees over toes, keep the object close to your body, stand using leg strength. Repeat with objects at different heights.

tips: Always engage core BEFORE lifting
Keep objects close to your body
Never twist while lifting
modifications: Use very light objects only

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Daily check of support garment.
activities.instructions: Assess your comfort and support needs.

tips: You may be ready to reduce wear time — consult your provider
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: True core strength means coordinating multiple muscle groups together. This week introduces exercises that require your core, breathing, and limbs to work as a team — just like they do in real life.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Develop multi-muscle coordination with core-centered movement patterns.

activities.name: Bird Dog Prep
activities.description: From hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg while keeping your core stable.
activities.instructions: Start on hands and knees, spine neutral. Engage your core. Slowly extend your right arm forward and left leg back. Hold for 5 seconds. Return to start. Switch sides. Keep your hips level throughout.

tips: Imagine balancing a cup of water on your lower back
Move slowly and with control
Your hips should not rotate or drop
modifications: Extend arm only, or leg only, if both is too challenging
Place a pillow under knees for comfort

activities.name: Coordinated Breathing
activities.description: Synchronize breathing with core exercises for integrated practice.
activities.instructions: During each core exercise today, consciously coordinate your breath: exhale during the effort phase, inhale during the release. Focus on making breathing and movement one fluid action.

tips: This is a skill that improves with practice
Don't force it — let it become natural
Notice how breathing supports your movement
modifications: Practice the coordination lying down first

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Continue 20-minute walks with improved awareness.
activities.instructions: Walk for 20 minutes. Today, focus on the coordination of your walking: arm swing, core engagement, breathing rhythm. Notice how everything works together.

tips: Walking is a coordination exercise in itself
Focus on smooth transitions between steps
Enjoy the rhythmic nature of walking
modifications: Adjust pace for comfort

activities.name: Daily Movement Audit
activities.description: Review how you move through common daily activities.
activities.instructions: Choose 5 common movements you do daily (getting out of bed, picking up a child, carrying groceries, etc.). Practice each one with conscious core engagement and proper body mechanics.

tips: Write down which movements feel easiest and hardest
Practice the hardest ones extra
Good habits now prevent problems later
modifications: Choose 3 movements if 5 feels like too many

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Daily support check.
activities.instructions: Continue monitoring support garment needs.

tips: Track how you feel with and without support
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: You've reached the halfway mark of your foundation phase! Take a moment to recognize your consistency and progress. Your body has been adapting and strengthening, even when you can't feel it day-to-day.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Celebrate your consistency, assess your progress, and prepare for the strengthening phase ahead.

activities.name: Core Strength Assessment
activities.description: Test your progress with a timed core hold and compare to Week 1.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent. Engage your core as deeply as you comfortably can. Hold for as long as possible while maintaining steady breathing. Record your time. Compare to your early-program experience. Then complete 3 sets of 12 reps of your core activation exercise.

tips: Don't push to discomfort — just notice improvement
Celebrate any progress, no matter how small
This is information, not judgment
modifications: If timed holds cause anxiety, skip the assessment and just do your regular sets

activities.name: Breathing Mastery Check
activities.description: Assess your breathing technique and practice advanced patterns.
activities.instructions: Spend 5 minutes practicing your best diaphragmatic breathing. Notice: Can you expand your ribcage in all directions? Can you coordinate breathing with movement naturally? Record your observations.

tips: This is a check-in, not a test
Notice improvements since Week 1
Breathing skills are life skills
modifications: Practice in your most comfortable position

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 20-minute walk with a progress mindset.
activities.instructions: Walk for 20 minutes. Reflect on how your walking has changed since Week 1. Is your posture better? Do you have more energy? Can you walk faster or further?

tips: Use this walk for reflection
Notice improvements in stamina
Consider journaling about your progress
modifications: Adjust duration as needed

activities.name: Body Mechanics Review
activities.description: Review all body mechanics learned so far.
activities.instructions: Practice hip hinges, proper lifting, sit-to-stand, and posture alignment. Do 5 repetitions of each. Notice which movements feel natural and which still need attention.

tips: Good form should be feeling more automatic
Identify any areas that need extra attention
Consistency is building lasting habits
modifications: Focus on the movements most relevant to your daily life

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Midpoint assessment of support needs.
activities.instructions: Assess whether your support garment needs are changing. You may need less support than when you started.

tips: Discuss changes with your healthcare provider
Progress may mean less reliance on external support
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: With a solid foundation, your body is ready for more challenging exercises. This phase focuses on building functional strength — the kind that helps you in everyday life, not just during exercises.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Transition from foundation exercises to strength-building movements with confidence.

activities.name: Bridge Exercise
activities.description: Lift your hips off the floor to engage glutes and deep core together.
activities.instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Engage your core. Press through your heels to lift your hips until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Hold for 5 seconds. Lower slowly. Repeat.

tips: Squeeze your glutes at the top
Don't arch your back — stay in a straight line
Keep your core engaged throughout
modifications: Reduce hold time if needed
Don't lift as high if uncomfortable

activities.name: Breathing Under Load
activities.description: Practice maintaining breathing patterns during more challenging exercises.
activities.instructions: During your bridge exercise, focus on exhaling as you lift and inhaling as you lower. This trains your body to breathe properly during effort — a skill many people lose.

tips: Never hold your breath during exercise
Exhale during the hard part
This becomes automatic with practice
modifications: Practice the breathing pattern without the exercise first

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: Increase walking to 22 minutes with varied terrain if possible.
activities.instructions: Walk for 22 minutes. If available, include stairs or hills. Maintain core engagement and proper posture throughout.

tips: Stairs are excellent for building leg and core strength
Go at your own pace on inclines
Use a handrail on stairs if needed
modifications: Stay on flat ground if inclines are uncomfortable

activities.name: Functional Strength Practice
activities.description: Apply your strength to daily tasks with proper form.
activities.instructions: Practice carrying a moderately weighted bag (groceries, books) with proper posture and core engagement. Walk 50 steps, set down properly, rest, repeat.

tips: Keep the weight close to your body
Distribute weight evenly if using two bags
Core engagement should be automatic by now
modifications: Use lighter weights
Reduce distance

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Monitor support needs during strengthening phase.
activities.instructions: Check if your support garment is still needed during exercise. You may find you need it less.

tips: Some people transition away from support during this phase
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: Functional strength means your core works automatically during real movements — reaching, carrying, pushing, pulling. The exercises this week mimic everyday patterns to build practical, usable strength.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Build strength that directly transfers to daily activities and movements.

activities.name: Side-Lying Core Work
activities.description: Strengthen your obliques and lateral core stabilizers.
activities.instructions: Lie on your side with knees bent. Prop yourself on your elbow. Lift your hips slightly off the floor and hold for 5 seconds. Lower gently. Do all reps on one side, then switch.

tips: Keep your body in a straight line from head to knees
Don't let your hips roll forward or back
Breathe steadily throughout
modifications: Keep knees bent for easier version
Reduce hold time to 3 seconds

activities.name: Breath Coordination
activities.description: Advanced breathing integrated with all exercises.
activities.instructions: For every exercise today, maintain conscious breath coordination: exhale during exertion, inhale during rest. Notice when you naturally hold your breath and redirect.

tips: Breath holding during effort is a common habit to break
You're retraining an automatic pattern
Be patient with yourself
modifications: Focus on one exercise at a time

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 25-minute walk at a moderate pace.
activities.instructions: Walk for 25 minutes at a pace that slightly elevates your heart rate. Maintain excellent posture throughout.

tips: You're building cardiovascular fitness too
A brisk walk is excellent exercise
Stay consistent — rain or shine
modifications: Split into smaller segments if needed

activities.name: Carrying & Reaching
activities.description: Practice carrying objects and reaching overhead with core control.
activities.instructions: Practice reaching to high shelves with core engaged. Practice carrying objects at different heights. Do 5 reaches and 5 carries, focusing on core stability.

tips: Engage core before reaching
Keep objects close to your body
Avoid twisting under load
modifications: Use very light objects

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Weekly support assessment.
activities.instructions: Assess support garment usage and comfort.

tips: Track your usage patterns
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: Your muscles grow stronger when challenged progressively. This week increases difficulty slightly — more reps, longer holds, or new movement patterns. Trust the process and listen to your body.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Accept increased exercise challenges while maintaining excellent form.

activities.name: Advanced Bridge
activities.description: Single-leg bridge variation for increased core challenge.
activities.instructions: Perform a bridge as practiced. At the top, slowly extend one leg straight. Hold for 3 seconds. Lower the leg, then lower your hips. Alternate legs.

tips: Keep your hips level when extending the leg
This is significantly harder — reduce reps if needed
Quality matters more than quantity
modifications: Keep both feet down and just practice longer holds
Extend leg only partially

activities.name: Standing Breathing
activities.description: Practice full breathing technique while standing and during activity.
activities.instructions: Stand tall and practice 360-degree breathing for 3 minutes. Then walk slowly for 2 minutes maintaining the breathing pattern. Total: 5 minutes of focused breath work.

tips: Standing breathing is more challenging than lying
This transfers to all daily activities
Practice during calm moments
modifications: Start with seated practice, progress to standing

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 25-minute walk with intervals of increased pace.
activities.instructions: Walk for 25 minutes. Every 5 minutes, increase your pace for 1 minute, then return to normal. This builds cardiovascular endurance alongside core strength.

tips: The fast intervals should feel challenging but manageable
Maintain posture even at higher speeds
This is the beginning of interval training
modifications: Skip intervals and maintain steady pace

activities.name: Multi-Plane Movement
activities.description: Practice core engagement during rotational and multi-directional movements.
activities.instructions: Practice gentle trunk rotation while standing (like looking over your shoulder). Practice side-stepping. Practice reaching across your body. All with conscious core engagement.

tips: Rotation should come from your thoracic spine, not your lower back
Move smoothly and with control
These movements are essential for daily life
modifications: Reduce range of motion
Hold onto a support

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Ongoing support assessment.
activities.instructions: Continue to monitor and adjust as needed.

tips: Many people are reducing support time by now
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: Integration means your exercises now flow together as connected movements rather than isolated actions. Your core, breathing, and movement patterns are becoming a coordinated system.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Connect all learned skills into flowing, integrated movement sequences.

activities.name: Flow Sequence
activities.description: Connect core exercises into a flowing sequence: activation, heel slides, marching, bridge.
activities.instructions: Perform exercises in sequence without resting between them: 5 core activations → 5 heel slides per side → 5 marches per side → 5 bridges. Rest 60 seconds. Repeat the flow.

tips: Maintain breathing throughout the entire flow
Transitions should be smooth, not rushed
This mimics how your body works in real life
modifications: Rest between exercises if needed
Reduce to 3 reps of each exercise

activities.name: Breath Flow
activities.description: Continuous breathing practice integrated with movement flow.
activities.instructions: During your exercise flow, maintain a 4-7 breathing pattern. Notice how your breath supports each movement transition. This is the ultimate mind-body coordination.

tips: This is a skill that takes practice
Don't get frustrated if coordination breaks down
Each attempt builds the neural pathway
modifications: Focus on breathing for just one exercise in the flow

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 25 minutes with integrated posture and core awareness.
activities.instructions: Walk for 25 minutes. Focus on the integration of all elements: posture, core engagement, breathing, arm swing. Notice how everything works together naturally now.

tips: Your walking should feel more effortless than Week 1
Notice improvements in stamina and posture
Walking is your daily maintenance exercise
modifications: Adjust pace as needed

activities.name: Real-Life Scenarios
activities.description: Practice complete real-life movement scenarios with proper mechanics.
activities.instructions: Practice these complete scenarios: 1) Get up from floor to standing. 2) Carry a laundry basket across a room. 3) Load/unload a dishwasher. 4) Pick up a child or pet. Use proper core engagement and body mechanics for each.

tips: These are the movements that matter most
Good mechanics prevent re-injury
Practice makes permanent
modifications: Choose scenarios relevant to your life
Use lighter loads

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Support assessment.
activities.instructions: Evaluate your current support needs.

tips: Integration phase often means less external support needed
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: You've been building strength for weeks. Now it's time to feel confident in your body's abilities. This week's exercises are more dynamic, building power and trust in your core.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Build confidence in your core strength through more dynamic and challenging exercises.

activities.name: Dynamic Bridge
activities.description: Add controlled tempo to bridge exercises for increased challenge.
activities.instructions: Perform bridges with a 3-second lift, 3-second hold, 3-second lower. This controlled tempo increases time under tension and builds real strength. Complete all reps with this rhythm.

tips: Tempo training is very effective
Count in your head: lift-2-3, hold-2-3, lower-2-3
Maintain breathing throughout
modifications: Reduce tempo to 2-2-2
Reduce reps to 8

activities.name: Power Breathing
activities.description: Short, powerful exhales paired with core engagement.
activities.instructions: Stand tall. Take a deep breath in. Exhale forcefully through pursed lips while contracting your core strongly, as if blowing out 50 birthday candles. Relax and repeat. This builds explosive core engagement.

tips: This is a different kind of breathing exercise
The exhale should be strong and short
You should feel your abs engage firmly
modifications: Use less force if uncomfortable
Practice seated

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 28-minute walk with confidence.
activities.instructions: Walk for 28 minutes at a brisk pace. Walk with confidence — shoulders back, head high, core strong. You've earned this posture.

tips: Notice how your walking has transformed
You should feel stronger and more capable
Celebrate this progress
modifications: Reduce to 25 minutes if needed

activities.name: Confidence Movements
activities.description: Practice movements that previously felt difficult or scary.
activities.instructions: Identify 3 movements that felt difficult or scary at the start of the program. Practice each one 5 times with proper form. Notice how much easier they feel now.

tips: This is about building trust in your body
Progress isn't always linear — celebrate where you are
Confidence comes from competence
modifications: Choose movements that feel safe to practice

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Ongoing support evaluation.
activities.instructions: Assess and adjust as needed.

tips: Many people are support-free by now during daily activities
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: Resilience is the ability to handle life's physical demands without setback. This week builds the endurance and strength that protects you during unexpected physical challenges — sneezing, stumbling, carrying heavy loads.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Build physical resilience that protects you during unexpected movements and challenges.

activities.name: Plank Progression
activities.description: Modified plank position to build full-core endurance.
activities.instructions: From hands and knees, walk your knees back slightly so your body forms a straight line from head to knees. Hold this modified plank position for 15 seconds. Rest. Repeat. Keep your core tight and back straight.

tips: Don't let your hips sag
Keep your head in line with your spine
Breathe steadily — don't hold your breath
modifications: Hold for 10 seconds instead of 15
Stay on hands and knees with core engaged

activities.name: Resilience Breathing
activities.description: Quick core engagement with unexpected breathing cues.
activities.instructions: Throughout the day, practice engaging your core quickly: before a cough, sneeze, laugh, or when startled. This trains your core to protect you automatically. Also complete 10 slow breaths.

tips: This is called 'bracing' — it protects your spine
Practice the quick engagement at random times
It should become reflexive
modifications: Focus on the slow breaths if quick engagement is difficult

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 30-minute walk — a major milestone.
activities.instructions: Walk for 30 minutes at a brisk pace. This is a major milestone! A 30-minute daily walk is one of the best things you can do for your overall health.

tips: 30 minutes is a key health milestone
Consider making this a permanent habit
Notice how far you can go now compared to Week 1
modifications: Split into three 10-minute walks

activities.name: Reactive Core Training
activities.description: Practice engaging your core quickly in response to sudden movements.
activities.instructions: Have someone gently push your shoulder or tap your back while you're standing. Practice bracing your core in response. If alone, practice quick core engagement when changing directions during walking.

tips: This trains automatic protection
Your core should respond before you think about it
Start gentle
modifications: Practice without a partner by quickly changing walking direction

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Support evaluation.
activities.instructions: Continue monitoring support needs.

tips: Your body is likely much stronger than when you started
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: You've built a strong foundation and are now capable of more advanced exercises. These movements challenge your core in new ways, building the deep strength that lasts long after this program ends.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Successfully perform advanced exercises that would have been impossible in Week 1.

activities.name: Full Bird Dog
activities.description: Full bird dog with extended holds and controlled movement.
activities.instructions: From hands and knees, extend opposite arm and leg fully. Hold for 8 seconds. Return slowly. Alternate sides. Add a gentle trunk rotation at the top of each hold — bring elbow to knee, then re-extend.

tips: This is an advanced exercise — be proud you can do it
The elbow-to-knee addition builds dynamic stability
Keep your core engaged throughout
modifications: Skip the elbow-to-knee rotation
Reduce hold to 5 seconds

activities.name: Advanced Breathing Integration
activities.description: Breathing mastery during challenging movements.
activities.instructions: During all exercises today, focus on breath mastery: no breath holding, smooth transitions, power exhales during effort. Rate your breathing coordination on a scale of 1-10 after each exercise.

tips: At this stage, breathing should be nearly automatic
Self-assessment builds awareness
Aim for 8/10 or higher
modifications: Focus on one exercise at a time

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 30-minute walk with power intervals.
activities.instructions: Walk for 30 minutes. Every 5 minutes, walk as fast as you can for 30 seconds, then return to normal pace. This builds cardiovascular fitness.

tips: Power intervals should feel challenging
Maintain posture during fast walking
Cool down with the last 5 minutes at an easy pace
modifications: Reduce interval intensity
Skip intervals and maintain steady pace

activities.name: Complex Daily Tasks
activities.description: Practice complex daily movements that require advanced core control.
activities.instructions: Practice these complex movements: 1) Carry two bags of groceries up stairs. 2) Vacuum or mop a floor. 3) Get up from the floor without using your hands. All with proper core engagement.

tips: These tasks test your real-world readiness
Getting up from the floor without hands is a great fitness test
Modify any task that doesn't feel safe
modifications: Use lighter loads
Use hands for floor-to-stand

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Late-program support evaluation.
activities.instructions: Assess your support needs as you approach program completion.

tips: Most people have significantly reduced or stopped using support
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: Mastery doesn't mean perfection — it means your core works for you automatically in daily life. This week focuses on establishing a sustainable maintenance routine you'll continue after the program ends.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Identify your personal maintenance routine that you'll continue beyond this program.

activities.name: Personal Best Challenge
activities.description: Attempt your personal best on key exercises.
activities.instructions: Today, try for your personal best: maximum core hold time, maximum plank hold, maximum bridge hold. Record your numbers. Then complete your regular routine: 3 sets of 12 bridges with 3-second tempo.

tips: Personal bests are personal — don't compare
Record your numbers for future reference
These numbers show your real progress
modifications: Skip the personal best attempt and do regular routine

activities.name: Maintenance Breathing
activities.description: Establish a sustainable daily breathing practice.
activities.instructions: Practice 5 minutes of your best breathing technique. Decide: what breathing practice will you maintain daily after the program? This is about building a lifelong habit.

tips: Even 2 minutes of breathing practice daily is beneficial
Choose a time that works for your schedule
Consistency matters more than duration
modifications: Start with 3 minutes

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 30-minute maintenance walk.
activities.instructions: Walk for 30 minutes. This is now your maintenance level. A daily 30-minute walk is one of the most powerful health habits you can maintain.

tips: Make walking a permanent part of your day
Find ways to walk more naturally — take stairs, park farther
Walking is medicine
modifications: Adjust duration to what's sustainable for you

activities.name: Movement Quality Assessment
activities.description: Assess the quality of your daily movements.
activities.instructions: Observe yourself throughout the day. Rate your movement quality in these areas: posture, lifting mechanics, core engagement during tasks, breathing during effort. Identify one area for continued focus.

tips: Self-assessment is a lifelong skill
Be honest but kind with yourself
Identify your strongest area and your growth area
modifications: Focus on just one area

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Final program phase support check.
activities.instructions: Evaluate your support needs as you prepare for independent exercise.

tips: You should feel confident in your body's ability to support itself
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: You're nearly at the end of the structured program. This week is about building confidence in your ability to continue independently. You have all the knowledge and skills — now it's about trusting yourself.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Design and practice your personal post-program exercise routine.

activities.name: Custom Core Routine
activities.description: Build your own 15-minute core routine from exercises you've learned.
activities.instructions: Choose your 4-5 favorite core exercises from the program. Arrange them in a flow that works for you. Practice your custom routine today. This is the routine you'll maintain.

tips: Choose exercises you enjoy — you'll do them more consistently
Include at least one from each difficulty level
Write down your routine
modifications: Use fewer exercises if needed
Include rest periods

activities.name: Breath Awareness
activities.description: Check your natural breathing patterns throughout the day.
activities.instructions: At three random points today, stop and observe your breathing without changing it. Is your breathing deep or shallow? Belly or chest? Fast or slow? Then do 10 corrective breaths.

tips: This builds lifelong breath awareness
Most people breathe too shallowly
Good breathing is the foundation of good health
modifications: Set phone reminders for the three check-ins

activities.name: Walking
activities.description: 30-minute independent walk.
activities.instructions: Walk for 30 minutes. Today, walk without thinking about posture or core engagement. Notice: does your body maintain good habits automatically? That's the sign of true learning.

tips: Automatic good posture means the program worked
Enjoy the walk — no mental effort required
Walking should feel natural and enjoyable
modifications: Any duration that works for you

activities.name: Daily Life Integration
activities.description: Observe how your body mechanics have become automatic in daily life.
activities.instructions: Go about your normal day and observe: Are you using good body mechanics automatically? Note 5 moments where your training kicked in without thinking. Celebrate each one.

tips: Automatic behavior change is the goal of the entire program
You've rewired movement patterns
Be proud of this achievement
modifications: Focus on observing just morning activities

activities.name: Splint or Binder Check
activities.description: Pre-completion support assessment.
activities.instructions: Final assessment of support garment needs before program completion.

tips: Most graduates of this program no longer need external support
modifications: Skip if not applicable

weeks.educationalContent: You did it. Eighteen weeks of consistent, dedicated rehabilitation. Your core is stronger, your movement patterns are healthier, and your body awareness is transformed. This isn't the end — it's the beginning of a stronger life.
weeks.weeklyGoal: Celebrate your achievement, establish your maintenance plan, and look forward with confidence.

activities.name: Final Assessment
activities.description: Complete your final strength assessment and celebrate your progress.
activities.instructions: Perform your personal best attempts: core hold, plank hold, bridge hold. Compare to your Week 8 numbers. Then perform your custom core routine one final time as a structured program exercise. After today, it's YOUR routine.

tips: This is a celebration, not a test
Compare to YOUR starting point, not anyone else's
You've accomplished something remarkable
modifications: Do whatever feels right for your body today

activities.name: Gratitude Breathing
activities.description: A breathing session focused on gratitude and accomplishment.
activities.instructions: Find a quiet place. Spend 5 minutes breathing deeply and reflecting on your journey. With each exhale, let go of any remaining tension or worry. With each inhale, breathe in confidence and gratitude for your body's ability to heal.

tips: This is your practice — take it with you
Breathing is always available to you
You've built a skill for life
modifications: Any comfortable position

activities.name: Celebration Walk
activities.description: A 30-minute walk to celebrate your journey.
activities.instructions: Walk for 30 minutes — but today, make it special. Walk somewhere beautiful if you can. Reflect on how far you've come. Notice how your body feels compared to Day 1. This is your celebration.

tips: Choose a route that makes you happy
Walk with someone who supported your journey
Take a moment to feel proud
modifications: Any duration that feels celebratory

activities.name: Future Movement Plan
activities.description: Write down your maintenance plan for continued core health.
activities.instructions: In your daily notes, write down: 1) Your maintenance exercise routine. 2) Your daily walking plan. 3) Your breathing practice schedule. 4) One body mechanics habit you'll maintain forever. This is your forward plan.

tips: A written plan is much more likely to be followed
Keep it simple and sustainable
Review your plan monthly
modifications: Dictate to a voice memo if writing is difficult

activities.name: Support Graduation
activities.description: Final support garment assessment and graduation.
activities.instructions: If you've been using a support garment, discuss with your healthcare provider about next steps. Many program graduates no longer need external support. Celebrate this independence.

tips: Your internal strength has replaced external support
Continue checking in with your body
Congratulations on completing the program
modifications: Skip if not applicable
